# mutis

> mutis is an open-source (MIT) encrypted file-sharing service. Files are encrypted in the browser (AES-256-GCM, WebCrypto) before upload; the server stores only ciphertext and never receives keys. Each file has an exit rule: once, a number of opens, a set time, or until deleted, and the server deletes the ciphertext when the rule says so. A file's key can be sent to a Tari address sealed inside a stealth TARI payment that only the recipient's keys open. Anyone can leave a file for a mutis user through a dead-drop link; deliveries travel on Tari Ootle sealed to the recipient's owner and view keys. A payment is credited only after a Tari-run public indexer confirms it on the Ootle and, where the deployment runs the proof sidecar, the official Tari library has proven its amount ({{ORIGIN}}/pricing says which). Runs on the Esmeralda testnet; tTARI has no monetary value. Independent project, not affiliated with Tari Labs.

The live limits (file sizes, expiry, views, prices) are in the public configuration: {{ORIGIN}}/api/v1/config
